evidence: Cut the data platform's cost by more than 50% through a FinOps effort
Reduced incidents and rework by ~3x by rolling out CI/CD with trunk-based
platform-wide observability and near-real-time business metrics monitoring (latency of a few minutes)
Led the migration of the company's entire data infrastructure to Databricks, bringing together ~50 sources
taking pipelines from hours to minutes
Built the company's dimensional model and data lake from scratch
including cost forecasting models to reduce spend in a predictable way
Helped create the company's LTV and payback models
prototypes in Lovable to dashboards in Streamlit and Metabase
Also contributed to the regulatory process that allowed the company to operate legally in Brazil
Grew the data group from 4 to ~20 people
Led the implementation of dbt on Redshift
Built 10+ APIs for sending data to partners and third parties
Architected the data protection processes (in compliance with LGPD)
Taught Big Data and Data Engineering courses to hundreds of students

claims.note: Confirmed by the owner in chat (not in the LinkedIn export): the data platform annual spend before the FinOps cut was in the six figures, in USD. A range only: never publish an exact value or a sharper range without asking.

Confirmed by the owner in chat (not in the LinkedIn export): a range only (thousands). Never publish an exact number or a sharper range without asking. Subject: people who use the platform (active users): thousands.

Confirmed by the owner in chat (not in the LinkedIn export): a range only (thousands). Never publish an exact number or a sharper range without asking. Subject: tables or datasets on the platform: thousands; jobs or pipeline runs per day: thousands.

Confirmed by the owner in chat (not in the LinkedIn export): these tools run in production on the data platform: Spark/PySpark, Delta Lake, Databricks Workflows, streaming, Terraform, Docker/Kubernetes, GitHub Actions. Shown as technologies of the platform roles and as skills; do not attach them to a specific project or case without asking.

Confirmed by the owner in chat (not in the LinkedIn export): the LTV and payback models were used to decide acquisition spend, estimate return and payback time, segment customers and evaluate campaigns; built in SQL/dbt with statistical and ML modeling, refreshed automatically by pipelines, shown in dashboards. His part: the input data and architecture, the pipelines and platform, and validating with data science and the business. Result: marketing got a numeric basis to decide where to invest. He did NOT say he led the team that built them or that he built the ML himself: do not claim it.

Confirmed by the owner in chat (not in the LinkedIn export): he uses generative AI in code (SQL, dbt, Python), documentation and data quality tests, natural-language assistants and queries, and data analysis (besides Lovable prototypes and Streamlit/Metabase dashboards); he introduced it to the team, set the usage guidelines and built AI solutions for the company. Tools he named: OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor, DeepSeek, GLM ("etc.": the list is not exhaustive, name only these). Effects he chose: faster prototypes, less repetitive work, more people building tools. He did NOT give numbers, nor the content of the guidelines: do not invent either.

Confirmed by the owner in chat (not in the LinkedIn export), as selections from a list: what weighed in choosing Databricks (one platform for batch, ML and BI; governance with Unity Catalog; cost and performance; the team's skills); the alternatives considered (staying on Redshift and the native AWS stack, Snowflake, BigQuery / Google Cloud); the biggest risks and trade-offs of the ~50-source migration (migrating without stopping the business, data parity, cost during the transition); and what he would do differently (start FinOps earlier, define domains and owners earlier). Say 'considered', never that any alternative was tested, priced or ruled out for a stated reason. He did NOT say Databricks was cheaper or faster than the alternatives, gave no numbers, no dates and no names of who decided: do not invent any of these.

claims.note: Confirmed by the owner in chat (not in the LinkedIn export), as selections from a list: what he prioritized in the FinOps effort (visibility of spend, the biggest cost drivers, cluster sizing, job scheduling); the trade-offs he had to manage (cost against data freshness, cost against performance, autonomy against rules, engineering time against savings); what kept the savings predictable and in place (cost forecasting models, cost attributed by domain or owner, spend alerts and dashboards, policies and guardrails); and what he would do differently besides starting earlier (tag and attribute cost by domain and owner from day one, automatic spend alerts earlier, involve the domains earlier). metrics._comment: Numbers allowed to appear with a unit/prefix (%, x, +, ~, >) anywhere on site/CV. Anything of that shape that is NOT here fails G3 (catches invented numbers).

forbidden._comment: Stale or private strings. scope: site | cv | all. Checked against rendered text (EN and PT) and raw HTML/JSON-LD. Exact private values (phone, birth date) live in the git-ignored _tools/fixtures/private-forbidden.json and are merged in by loadFacts().
